blurb: Glossy solid-black cat with copper eyes, bred to look like a mini panther
description: The Bombay is a short-haired cat breed from the United States, a medium-sized muscular cat with a glossy jet-black coat, copper-gold eyes and a social nature.
answer: The Bombay is a short-haired domestic cat breed developed in the United States from the late 1950s to resemble a miniature black panther. It is a medium-sized, muscular cat of about 2.5 to 5 kg with a sleek solid black coat and copper-golden eyes, and is described as highly social.

body: The US-type Bombay was developed by Nikki Horner of Louisville, Kentucky, starting in 1958, by crossing sable American Burmese with black American Shorthairs; her second attempt, in 1965, succeeded. The breed is named after the city of Bombay (Mumbai), a reference to the Indian black leopard. The CFA recognized it in 1970 and TICA in 1979, while FIFe gives it only preliminary status. A separate UK type, registered by the GCCF as the Asian Self, arose from matings of European Burmese with black shorthairs. Both types are relatively rare.

The Bombay is closely related to the Burmese. It has a medium, graceful, muscular body, a rounded short head with a short muzzle, and medium, wide-set ears with rounded tips. The coat is short, dense, close-lying and glossy, solid black to the roots, with black whiskers, skin, paw pads and nose leather. The large round eyes are always copper to golden; green is not allowed. Females average about 2.5 to 3.5 kg and males about 3.5 to 5 kg.

The Bombay is commonly described as highly social, strongly attached to its family and craving attention, traits often said to make it suitable for homes with children. Many are said to prefer quieter surroundings.
Bombays are noted to do well as strictly indoor cats, even in a small apartment, as long as their needs are met. Sources give little further care detail.

A healthy Bombay is reported to live about 15 years on average, with some reaching 20. Conditions reported in the breed include nasal and sinus problems and gingivitis. Regular veterinary check-ups are recommended.

faq.q: How long do Bombay cats live?
faq.a: Healthy Bombays are reported to live about 15 years on average, and some have reached 20.

faq.q: Are Bombay cats good with children?
faq.a: They are commonly described as social, family-attached and attention-seeking, which is why they are often called suitable for children; individuals vary.

faq.q: How big does a Bombay cat get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat weighing about 2.5 to 5 kg, with males usually heavier than females.
